settings.initial_guess: zero vector in every independent parameter solve
settings.branch: smooth lower branch, alpha=1 and alpha=2; no folds or branch switching validated
settings.derivative_construction: Forward AD of shared residual in augmented coordinates (u,lambda); no Newton iteration unrolling
settings.adjoint_convention: Euclidean discrete gradient; p contains h weighting and is not directly a continuum adjoint nodal value
settings.residual_norms: unscaled residual Euclidean norms; relative sensitivity denominator ||F_lambda||2, adjoint denominator ||L_u||2
settings.finite_difference: central parameter difference with separate zero-start nonlinear solves at lambda +/- epsilon
settings.continuous_reference: Differentiate exact alpha-family; independent 96/192-point Gauss integral for continuum objective derivative

continuous_references.definition: beta*lambda + integral_0^1 u_alpha(x)*(du_alpha/dlambda)(x) dx; exact continuous family
beta*lambda + integral_0^1 u_alpha(x)*(du_alpha/dlambda)(x) dx; exact continuous family

nonsymmetric_check.objective: w dot u + .5 theta.T R theta
nonsymmetric_check.reason: Bratu Jacobian is symmetric; this independent three-state/two-parameter system detects wrong transpose and sign conventions.

scope: Real, finite-dimensional implicit differentiation and discrete adjoints for smooth lower-branch Bratu. Original AD/Newton code retained. Dense linear solves, one physical parameter and one scalar objective. An independent nonsymmetric multiparameter manufactured system tests the transpose and sign. No reverse-mode AD engine, nonlinear-iteration differentiation, PDE-constrained inverse fit, time-dependent/continuous-adjoint solver, singular fold continuation, or performance ranking. Primal, derivative and continuum errors are distinct.
